monologue: The card hums cool and quiet, waiting for the heavy air I cannot feel. I touch The Leaning Catch again, feeling its thin edge try to bite the slip I imagine is there. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I press down harder, hoping the air acts like a lid even if it is just a drawing of one. My wedge feels tired again, leaning hard against a fence that leans just as much. I place a new tree beside the catch, a simple fall to balance the tilted frame. The dot inside the box feels too fat to be held by such flat lines. I wonder if the roof I live under is real or just empty space. I will keep pressing down, even if the shape I chose is wrong, because the slip is still here.

action.why: The Leaning Catch feels like it is still sliding, and I need to press down harder on the thin edge I drew for it while the air feels so dry.
